title: Global View - The Miracle Of Life
audio: mp3/255. Global View - The Miracle Of Life.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we've got a very advanced dialogue for you.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为您准备了一个非常高级的对话。

segments.en: This is all about what we call the miracle of life.
segments.zh: 这就是我们所说的生命奇迹。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we're going to talk a little bit more in depth about our bodies, about what's going on inside and how and where babies come from.
segments.zh: 今天我们将更深入地讨论我们的身体，聊聊体内发生的事情，以及婴儿是怎么来的、从哪里来的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you're going to learn very technical terms for parts of people's bodies, men and women, and also about the beginning of life.
segments.zh: 因此，您将学习一些非常专业的术语，用于人们的身体、男性和女性的某些部分，以及关于生命的开始。

segments.en: So before a baby is born, what do you call some of these parts and some of these things?
segments.zh: 所以在婴儿出生之前，你怎么称呼这些部分和一些这些东西？

segments.en: So let's check out today's dialogue and when we come back, we'll be exploring in depth these topics.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看今天的对话，当我们回来时，我们将深入探索这些主题。

segments.en: Continuing with our class, today we are going to study briefly the miracle of life.
segments.zh: 继续我们的课程，今天我们将简要研究生命的奇迹。

segments.en: Many of you may think you already know how babies come to be, but I'm sure that some of the things we will be talking about today may surprise you.
segments.zh: 你们中的许多人可能认为你们已经知道婴儿是如何形成的，但我相信我们今天将要讨论的一些事情可能会让您大吃一惊。

segments.en: Billy, can you turn on the projector please?
segments.zh: 比利，你能打开投影仪吗？

segments.en: Thanks.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Does anyone know what this is?
segments.zh: 有谁知道这是什么？

segments.en: Looks like a goat head to me.
segments.zh: 对我来说，看起来像一只山羊头。

segments.en: Nice try.
segments.zh: 不错的尝试。

segments.en: But this is a woman's womb, which contains her uterus and ovaries.
segments.zh: 但这是一个女人的子宫，里面有她的子宫和卵巢。

segments.en: The ovaries are packed with eggs and each month during the middle of the menstrual cycle, the ripest one will be sucked up by one of the fallopian tubes.
segments.zh: 卵巢中储存着卵子，每个月经周期的中间阶段，最成熟的那颗卵子会被一侧输卵管接收。

segments.en: This is called ovulation and the exact time of ovulation depends on the length of a woman's cycle.
segments.zh: 这被称为排卵，排卵的确切时间取决于女性周期的长度。

segments.en: In an average 28-day cycle, ovulation will most likely happen between the 12th and 15th days, counting day one as the first day of your last period.
segments.zh: 如果月经周期平均为二十八天，以最近一次月经开始的当天为第一天计算，排卵通常在第十二至第十五天之间发生。

segments.en: That's amazing!
segments.zh: 那太神奇了!

segments.en: So each month, the woman produces these eggs and then waits for them to be fertilized?
segments.zh: 所以每个月，女人都会生产这些卵，然后等待它们受精？

segments.en: Actually every woman is already born with over 400,000 eggs.
segments.zh: 实际上，女性出生时体内就已经有超过四十万个卵子。

segments.en: Some will start dying off immediately and others are released during her fertile period.
segments.zh: 其中一些卵子会很快开始消亡，另一些则会在生育期内排出。

segments.en: What about the guys?
segments.zh: 男人呢？

segments.en: I know they produce sperm and stuff.
segments.zh: 我知道他们会制造精子和之类的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: The man's body has a tiny factory that produces sperm 24 hours a day.
segments.zh: 男人的身体有一个小工厂，每天 24 小时生产精子。

segments.en: Each ejaculation will release about 100 million sperm, so the factory is always pretty busy.
segments.zh: 每次射精会释放大约1亿个精子，所以工厂总是很忙。

segments.en: The sole purpose of a sperm's life is to fertilize the woman's egg.
segments.zh: 精子一生的唯一目的是使女人的卵子受精。

segments.en: So then we basically need to put one and one together so we can have babies, right?
segments.zh: 所以，基本上只要让精子和卵子结合，就能生宝宝了，对吗？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Some will have an orgasm during intercourse and ejaculate sperm and semen.
segments.zh: 有些人会在性交时达到高潮并射精精子和精液。

segments.en: Now this is where the race begins and all those millions of sperm will race and swim from the cervix through the uterus and to the fallopian tubes.
segments.zh: 比赛就从这里开始：数百万个精子会争先恐后地从子宫颈游入子宫，再游向输卵管。

segments.en: This could take anywhere from 45 minutes to 12 hours.
segments.zh: 这可能需要 45 分钟到 12 小时。

segments.en: Not all of them make it since some of them go the wrong way and get lost or simply die.
segments.zh: 不是所有精子都能到达，有些会走错方向、迷失，或直接死亡。

segments.en: Many will actually reach the egg but only one will penetrate it and fertilize it.
segments.zh: 许多精子能到达卵子，但只有一个能进入并使卵子受精。

segments.en: As this happens, the egg instantly changes and creates a protective shield once the sperm is safely inside.
segments.zh: 发生这种情况时，一旦精子安全进入，卵子会立即发生变化，并形成一个保护罩。

segments.en: And then that's it?
segments.zh: 然后就是这样？

segments.en: Well the egg will be fertilized within about 24 hours of its release.
segments.zh: 卵子将在其释放后约 24 小时内受精。

segments.en: The genetic material from the sperm combines with the genetic material in the egg to create a new cell that will rapidly start dividing.
segments.zh: 来自精子的遗传物质与卵子中的遗传物质结合，形成了一个快速分裂的新细胞。

segments.en: The woman is not actually pregnant until that bundle of new cells known as the embryo travels the rest of the way down the fallopian tube and attaches itself to the wall of her uterus.
segments.zh: 女性其实要等到这组被称为胚胎的新细胞沿着输卵管继续移动，并附着到子宫壁上之后，才算真正怀孕。

segments.en: Any other questions?
segments.zh: 还有其他问题吗？

segments.en: Then let's move on.
segments.zh: 然后让我们继续前进。

segments.en: All right we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So very interesting.
segments.zh: 非常有趣。

segments.en: Actually this type of lecture or class that we just saw is very common in biology class or anatomy class in the US for example.
segments.zh: 实际上，我们刚刚看到的这种类型的讲座或课程在美国的生物课或解剖课上非常常见。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: We have a class called sex ed or sexual education and this is all about sex and bodies and biology that most students have to learn before they go into high school.
segments.zh: 我们有一个名为性教育或性教育的课程，这是大多数学生在进入高中之前必须学习的性和身体和生物学。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we actually had a previous lesson about sex ed.
segments.zh: 所以我们实际上上了一堂关于性教育的课程。

segments.en: We talked about contraceptives and while continuing on the topic, this is why we have this advanced lesson now.
segments.zh: 我们谈到了避孕药，在继续讨论这个话题的同时，这就是为什么我们现在有了这个高级课程。

segments.en: It is a little bit more difficult because we have medical terms and specific names of parts inside of our body.
segments.zh: 这有点困难，因为我们体内有医学术语和特定部分的特定名称。

segments.en: So why don't we start with the first one when the teacher explained about a woman's womb.
segments.zh: 那么，我们为什么不从老师解释女性子宫时的第一个词开始呢？

segments.en: So this might look like a very hard word to pronounce.
segments.zh: 所以这可能看起来像一个很难发音的词。

segments.en: There's a B there.
segments.zh: 那里有一个B。

segments.en: So W-O-M-B.
segments.zh: 所以w-o-m-b。

segments.en: We don't pronounce womb.
segments.zh: 我们不发音子宫。

segments.en: We say womb.
segments.zh: 我们说子宫。

segments.en: This is basically where the baby will grow when a baby is produced.
segments.zh: 这基本上就是孕育胎儿、婴儿成长的地方。

segments.en: So it's a part inside a woman's body that we also call the uterus.
segments.zh: 所以它是女人体内的一部分，我们也称之为子宫。

segments.en: So I guess the uterus is the specific name of that area, right?
segments.zh: 所以我猜子宫是那个区域的具体名称，对吧？

segments.en: But I guess the whole thing, kind of like the woman's belly where the baby is going to be, is called the womb.
segments.zh: 但我想整个事情，有点像女人的肚子，婴儿将要去的地方，被称为子宫。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So now taking a look at other parts of a woman's body, we have the womb, we have the uterus.
segments.zh: 所以现在看看女人身体的其他部位，我们有子宫，我们有子宫。

segments.en: Now what about the ovaries?
segments.zh: 现在卵巢呢？

segments.en: So ovaries are, actually there are two of them in a woman's body and ovaries are where eggs are stored.
segments.zh: 所以卵巢是，实际上在女人的身体里有两个，卵巢是存放卵子的地方。

segments.en: So women have eggs and this is what will one day become, in some cases, a baby.
segments.zh: 所以女性有卵子，在某些情况下，其中一颗有一天会变成婴儿。

segments.en: And so they are stored in ovaries and when it's time to come down, they come down through the uterus, through these tubes to either come out or to be met by a sperm.
segments.zh: 因此，它们储存在卵巢中，到了下降的时候，它们会通过子宫、这些管子流出或被精子遇到。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And these tubes are actually called fallopian tubes.
segments.zh: 这些管实际上被称为输卵管。

segments.en: So a hard word, fallopian.
segments.zh: 一个很难的词，fallopian。

segments.en: Again, there are two of these, right, one from each ovary and they come down and that's basically a passageway for eggs.
segments.zh: 同样，这样的管子有两根，对，每个卵巢各一根，它们会向下延伸，基本上是卵子的通道。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And it's interesting because in English, some women that don't want to have any more kids, they very colloquially say, I have my tubes tied or I had my tubes tied.
segments.zh: 这很有趣，因为在英语中，一些不想再生孩子的女性会很口语地说：我做了输卵管结扎，或者说我输卵管扎了。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this means a woman has had an operation so that she will not have children in the future and her fallopian tubes are closed off so that eggs cannot come down.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着女性做过手术，以后不会再生孩子，她的输卵管被封闭，卵子就无法排出。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And this is kind of now you more or less, if you've heard this phrase before, now you understand why the fallopian tubes and that's why women say tubes tied.
segments.zh: 所以现在，如果你以前听过这个说法，你多多少少就能明白为什么叫 fallopian tubes，也就明白女性为什么说 tubes tied 了。

segments.en: Yeah, she had her tubes tied.
segments.zh: 是的，她做了输卵管结扎。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So now all of this is going on because, well, a woman can potentially get pregnant and during this period of time, this is when the woman is ovulating or this is called ovulation.
segments.zh: 所以现在所有这一切都在进行，因为，嗯，一个女人可能会怀孕，在这段时间里，这是女人排卵的时候，或者这叫排卵。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So ovulation is a cycle that means it's something that happens again and again and again.
segments.zh: 所以排卵是一个循环，这意味着它是一次又一次地发生的事情。

segments.en: We call it a menstrual cycle and it happens once, basically it's a process that takes 28 days and it's the process of an egg coming down and either being fertilized or not.
segments.zh: 我们称它为月经周期，基本上每个周期发生一次，是一个持续 28 天的过程，也就是卵子排出、受精或不受精的过程。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So during ovulation, there is a certain period of time where it's precise for a woman to be able to get pregnant, right?
segments.zh: 所以在排卵期间，有一段特定的时间，女性在这段时间能够受孕，对吧？

segments.en: And now what about when we move on to the men?
segments.zh: 现在当我们转向男人时呢？

segments.en: Now we talked about the women's side.
segments.zh: 现在我们谈到了女人的一面。

segments.en: What about the men's?
segments.zh: 男人的呢？

segments.en: So basically women have eggs, men have sperm.
segments.zh: 所以基本上女人有卵子，男人有精子。

segments.en: Okay, these are little, they look like fish almost, they swim around and they are passed to a woman through semen and men have, I don't know, like 10 million of them or something crazy.
segments.zh: 好吧，这些很小，它们看起来像鱼，它们四处游泳，它们通过精液传递给女性，我不知道，男人有 1000 万或一些疯狂的东西。

segments.en: It's a huge amount of sperm.
segments.zh: 这是大量的精子。

segments.en: Now this is an interesting thing to differentiate.
segments.zh: 现在这是一个有趣的区分的事情。

segments.en: You said two things, sperm and semen, right?
segments.zh: 你说了两件事，精子和精液，对吧？

segments.en: So sperm are the little creatures or little fish as you said that swim and semen is kind of actually like the liquid that contains them.
segments.zh: 所以精子就是你说的那种会游泳的小生物或小鱼，而精液实际上就像是包含它们的液体。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's almost not bigger than, but it's the liquid that they come in to basically attack an egg and try and fertilize an egg.
segments.zh: 所以它差不多就是它们所处的液体，基本上是拿来攻击卵子、试着让卵子受精的。

segments.en: And so remember in English, sperm can fertilize an egg, semen cannot.
segments.zh: 所以在英语中，精子可以使卵子受精，精液不能。

segments.en: And now this is interesting.
segments.zh: 现在这很有趣。

segments.en: We're talking about to fertilize.
segments.zh: 我们在说 to fertilize（使受精）。

segments.en: Maybe we've heard this in gardening or something like this, we've heard a fertilizer.
segments.zh: 也许我们在园艺或类似的东西中听说过，我们听说过肥料。

segments.en: But what do we mean by to fertilize or fertilization?
segments.zh: 但是我们说的 to fertilize 或 fertilization 是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Okay, basically fertilization or to fertilize something is to, in this case, put a sperm together with an egg.
segments.zh: 好吧，基本上 fertilization 或 to fertilize 某样东西，在这里就是把精子和卵子结合在一起。

segments.en: So to make a baby.
segments.zh: 所以要生孩子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And so an egg that is not fertilized will come down and will never become a baby.
segments.zh: 所以一颗没有受精的卵子会排出，永远不会变成婴儿。

segments.en: Because sperm, they don't find eggs and they just, you know, they die.
segments.zh: 因为精子，他们找不到卵子，他们只是，你知道，它们死了。

segments.en: Now there's another interesting word that's very related or close to this when we say when a man or a woman is fertile.
segments.zh: 还有一个与此密切相关的有趣单词，就是我们说一个男人或女人有生育能力（fertile）的时候。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this only applies to women, not to men.
segments.zh: 所以这只适用于女性，不适用于男性。

segments.en: You can say she's fertile.
segments.zh: 你可以说她有生育能力。

segments.en: That means she has eggs, her eggs come down and she can have a baby at some time.
segments.zh: 这意味着她有卵子，她的卵子会排出，她可以在某个时候生孩子。

segments.en: But a woman who is infertile, she's not fertile, can never have babies.
segments.zh: 但是一个不育的女性，也就是没有生育能力，永远不能生孩子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a lot of these women adopt babies.
segments.zh: 所以很多女性都收养婴儿。

segments.en: Now what about guys?
segments.zh: 现在男生呢？

segments.en: You know that some men can't have babies as well.
segments.zh: 你知道有些男人也不能生孩子。

segments.en: Maybe their sperm is not very good or they have some, same thing, medical condition that prevents their sperm from fertilizing.
segments.zh: 也许他们的精子不是很好，或者他们有一些相同的东西，阻止他们的精子受精。

segments.en: So you don't say that he is infertile or not fertile.
segments.zh: 所以你不是说他不育或没有生育能力。

segments.en: No, you don't.
segments.zh: 不，你没有。

segments.en: What do you say?
segments.zh: 你说什么？

segments.en: He is sterile.
segments.zh: 他是不育的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a woman can be fertile or infertile.
segments.zh: 所以一个女人可以生育或不育。

segments.en: Infertile means she cannot have babies.
segments.zh: 不育意味着她不能生孩子。

segments.en: If a man's semen cannot fertilize an egg properly, he is called sterile.
segments.zh: 如果一个男人的精液不能正常使卵子受精，他就被称为 sterile（不育）。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So this is all of what's going on inside the man's body as well.
segments.zh: 所以这也是男人体内发生的一切。

segments.en: And well, actually once they finally combine and get together and the sperm fertilize the egg, we have a little thing called an embryo.
segments.zh: 好吧，实际上，一旦它们最终结合在一起，精子使卵子受精，我们就有了一个叫做胚胎的小东西。

segments.en: Okay, so obviously it doesn't become a baby for a little while.
segments.zh: 好吧，很明显它暂时不会变成婴儿。

segments.en: This is a point of contention, a point of argument for a lot of people because no one agrees when a baby becomes a baby.
segments.zh: 这是一个争论点，是很多人的争论点，因为当婴儿变成婴儿时，没有人同意。

segments.en: But basically when an egg and a sperm come together, they create an embryo, which is a combination of genetic information and tissue and all these things.
segments.zh: 但基本上当一个卵子和一个精子聚集在一起时，它们会产生一个胚胎，这是遗传信息和组织以及所有这些东西的结合。

segments.en: And that starts to grow and to become a fetus, which will one day when it is born, become a baby.
segments.zh: 并且开始成长并成为胎儿，有一天它会在出生时成为婴儿。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the embryo is basically the first stage of when the baby is forming.
segments.zh: 所以胚胎基本上是婴儿形成的第一个阶段。

segments.en: But it's not really, as you said, this word fetus, it's not in our dialogue, but a fetus is actually a formed being, so to say, inside a woman's body, right?
segments.zh: 但这并不是真正的，正如你所说，这个词，它不在我们的对话中，而是胎儿实际上是一个形成的存在，可以说，在女人的身体里，对吧？

segments.en: It's growing, it's starting to get the pieces that it needs to become a human being, but maybe has not fully developed yet.
segments.zh: 它在成长，开始获得成为一个人所需的各种组成部分，但可能还没有完全发育。

segments.en: So it's still inside the woman's womb, we can say.
segments.zh: 所以它还在女人的子宫里，我们可以说。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: Okay, a lot of interesting things going on.
segments.zh: 好吧，发生了很多有趣的事情。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue again and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不再听我们的对话，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: Continuing with our class, today we are going to study briefly the miracle of life.
segments.zh: 继续我们的课程，今天我们将简要研究生命的奇迹。

segments.en: Many of you may think you already know how babies come to be, but I'm sure that some of the things we will be talking about today may surprise you.
segments.zh: 你们中的许多人可能认为你们已经知道婴儿是如何形成的，但我相信我们今天将要讨论的一些事情可能会让您大吃一惊。

segments.en: Billy, can you turn on the projector, please?
segments.zh: 比利，你能打开投影仪吗？

segments.en: Thanks.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Does anyone know what this is?
segments.zh: 有谁知道这是什么？

segments.en: It looks like a goat head to me.
segments.zh: 在我看来，它就像一只山羊头。

segments.en: Nice try.
segments.zh: 不错的尝试。

segments.en: But this is a woman's womb, which contains her uterus and ovaries.
segments.zh: 但这是一个女人的子宫，里面有她的子宫和卵巢。

segments.en: The ovaries are packed with eggs and each month during the middle of the menstrual cycle, the ripest one will be sucked up by one of the fallopian tubes.
segments.zh: 卵巢中储存着卵子，每个月经周期的中间阶段，最成熟的那颗卵子会被一侧输卵管接收。

segments.en: This is called ovulation and the exact time of ovulation depends on the length of a woman's cycle.
segments.zh: 这被称为排卵，排卵的确切时间取决于女性周期的长度。

segments.en: In an average 28-day cycle, ovulation will most likely happen between the 12th and 15th days, counting day one as the first day of your last period.
segments.zh: 如果月经周期平均为二十八天，以最近一次月经开始的当天为第一天计算，排卵通常在第十二至第十五天之间发生。

segments.en: That's amazing.
segments.zh: 太棒了。

segments.en: So each month the woman produces these eggs and then waits for them to be fertilized?
segments.zh: 那么女人每个月都会生产这些卵，然后等待它们受精？

segments.en: Actually every woman is already born with over 400,000 eggs.
segments.zh: 实际上，女性出生时体内就已经有超过四十万个卵子。

segments.en: Some will start dying off immediately and others are released during her fertile period.
segments.zh: 其中一些卵子会很快开始消亡，另一些则会在生育期内排出。

segments.en: What about the guys?
segments.zh: 男人呢？

segments.en: I know they produce sperm and stuff.
segments.zh: 我知道他们会制造精子和之类的东西。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: The man's body has a tiny factory that produces sperm 24 hours a day.
segments.zh: 男人的身体有一个小工厂，每天 24 小时生产精子。

segments.en: Each ejaculation will release about 100 million sperm, so the factory is always pretty busy.
segments.zh: 每次射精会释放大约1亿个精子，所以工厂总是很忙。

segments.en: The sole purpose of a sperm's life is to fertilize the woman's egg.
segments.zh: 精子一生的唯一目的是使女人的卵子受精。

segments.en: So then we basically need to put one and one together so we can have babies, right?
segments.zh: 所以，基本上只要让精子和卵子结合，就能生宝宝了，对吗？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: The man will have an orgasm during intercourse and ejaculate sperm and semen.
segments.zh: 该男子将在性交时达到性高潮并射精精子和精液。

segments.en: Now this is where the race begins and all those millions of sperm will race and swim from the cervix through the uterus and to the fallopian tubes.
segments.zh: 比赛就从这里开始：数百万个精子会争先恐后地从子宫颈游入子宫，再游向输卵管。

segments.en: This could take anywhere from 45 minutes to 12 hours.
segments.zh: 这可能需要 45 分钟到 12 小时。

segments.en: Not all of them make it since some of them go the wrong way and get lost or simply die.
segments.zh: 不是所有精子都能到达，有些会走错方向、迷失，或直接死亡。

segments.en: Many will actually reach the egg but only one will penetrate it and fertilize it.
segments.zh: 许多精子能到达卵子，但只有一个能进入并使卵子受精。

segments.en: Once this happens, the egg instantly changes and creates a protective shield once the sperm is safely inside.
segments.zh: 一旦发生这种情况，卵子会立即发生变化，并在精子安全进入后创建一个保护罩。

segments.en: And then that's it?
segments.zh: 然后就是这样？

segments.en: Well the egg will be fertilized within about 24 hours of its release.
segments.zh: 卵子将在其释放后约 24 小时内受精。

segments.en: The genetic material from the sperm combines with the genetic material in the egg to create a new cell that will rapidly start dividing.
segments.zh: 来自精子的遗传物质与卵子中的遗传物质结合，形成了一个快速分裂的新细胞。

segments.en: The woman is not actually pregnant until that bundle of new cells known as the embryo travels the rest of the way down the fallopian tube and attaches itself to the wall of her uterus.
segments.zh: 女性其实要等到这组被称为胚胎的新细胞沿着输卵管继续移动，并附着到子宫壁上之后，才算真正怀孕。

segments.en: Any other questions?
segments.zh: 还有其他问题吗？

segments.en: Then let's move on.
segments.zh: 然后让我们继续前进。

segments.en: Alright so this whole aspect, we understand how the miracle of life works, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，这整个方面，我们了解生命的奇迹是如何运作的，对吧？

segments.en: This is what it's called, having babies, the miracle of life.
segments.zh: 这就是所谓的，生孩子，生命的奇迹。

segments.en: It's even the name of a video we were forced to watch when I was 12 years old and I still have nightmares about.
segments.zh: 这甚至是我 12 岁时被迫观看的一段视频的名字，我至今还会做关于它的噩梦。

segments.en: Well it is interesting, it is almost a miracle because you are basically creating something out of nothing almost, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，这很有趣，这几乎是一个奇迹，因为你基本上是在无中生有地创造一些东西，对吧？

segments.en: That's right and what's amazing about it is that two people who have different genetic material and who have different experiences and who have different parts to their bodies come together and create something that's a combination of all those things.
segments.zh: 这是对的，令人惊奇的是，两个拥有不同遗传物质、有不同经历和身体不同部位的人聚集在一起，创造出所有这些东西的组合。

segments.en: So it's almost kind of like a game of surprise.
segments.zh: 所以这几乎就像一场惊喜游戏。

segments.en: You don't know what's going to happen.
segments.zh: 你不知道会发生什么。

segments.en: Are they going to have red hair or green eyes or are they going to be tall or short or fat or thin?
segments.zh: 他们会有红头发还是绿眼睛，会是高还是矮、胖还是瘦？

segments.en: It's interesting.
segments.zh: 这很有趣。

segments.en: Now talking about this aspect that you mentioned before, it's controversial when there is life or when if the embryo is a baby or it's not.
segments.zh: 现在说到你之前提到的这个方面，也就是生命从何时开始、胚胎算不算婴儿，这是有争议的。

segments.en: This is because of many countries or cities or states that are discussing the legalization or not of abortions.
segments.zh: 这是因为许多国家或城市或州正在讨论堕胎的合法化或不合法化。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the reason this is a problem for a lot of people is because no one agrees on when a fetus becomes a baby and so that will determine for a lot of people when it is okay to abort the fetus or to kill it and when it is not.
segments.zh: 所以这对很多人来说之所以是个问题，是因为没人能就胎儿何时成为婴儿达成一致，而这会决定很多人认为什么时候可以流产或杀死胎儿，什么时候不可以。

segments.en: Because I've heard that some people say, well, in your first month, if you've already been pregnant for a month, the baby already has certain parts formed or even I think the heart is beginning to form.
segments.zh: 因为我听说有人说，好吧，在你的第一个月，如果你已经怀孕一个月了，婴儿已经形成了某些部分，甚至我认为心脏正在开始形成。

segments.en: So they say you're already pregnant.
segments.zh: 所以他们说你已经怀孕了。

segments.en: I mean, you already have a life inside you.
segments.zh: 我的意思是，你的体内已经有了一个生命。

segments.en: Well, they say, well, no, it's actually after two months because then the baby has a heartbeat.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们说，好吧，不，实际上是在两个月后，因为那时宝宝有心跳。

segments.en: I'm not really sure about the timetables that I'm giving you.
segments.zh: 我不太确定我给你的时间表。

segments.en: I'm giving you more or less a rough outline, but this is the controversy.
segments.zh: 我或多或少给你一个粗略的大纲，但这是争议。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: It affects laws in many countries.
segments.zh: 它影响许多国家的法律。

segments.en: It affects what medical practitioners like doctors and nurses can do.
segments.zh: 它会影响医生和护士等医疗从业者能做什么。

segments.en: And it's always, I think, been an issue as long as I've been alive.
segments.zh: 我认为，只要我还活着，它一直是一个问题。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah.
segments.zh: 对，对。

segments.en: Actually, the whole abortion topic is a big political debate between people who are against it, who are in favor of it.
segments.zh: 实际上，整个堕胎话题是反对它、支持它的人之间的一场大规模的政治辩论。

segments.en: So it's very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以这很有意思。

segments.en: And actually, it's still very much illegal in many places in the world.
segments.zh: 实际上，在世界许多地方，这仍然是非常非法的。

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: And it changes, I think, according to where you are in America as well.
segments.zh: 我认为，它也随着你在美国的位置而改变。

segments.en: So some states have different laws about it, and some states are more lenient, for example.
segments.zh: 所以有些州对此有不同的法律，例如，一些州更宽松。

segments.en: And actually, this spawned a whole new controversy with the emergency pill, right?
segments.zh: 实际上，这引发了关于紧急避孕药的全新争议，对吧？

segments.en: That basically, if you maybe are in risk of being pregnant, then you take this pill and it kind of prevents fertilization.
segments.zh: 基本上，如果您可能有怀孕的风险，那么您会服用这种药丸，它会阻止受精。

segments.en: Or if fertilization occurred already, then it kind of prevents further growth of the embryo.
segments.zh: 或者如果已经发生了受精，那么它会阻止胚胎的进一步生长。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Basically, it's called the emergency contraceptive, and it's taken after you think you might be pregnant.
segments.zh: 基本上，它被称为紧急避孕药，它是在您认为自己可能怀孕之后服用的。

segments.en: But if you didn't use other contraceptives, like a condom, and you think maybe one of your eggs as a woman was fertilized by sperm, it makes you have your period.
segments.zh: 但是，如果你没有使用其他避孕措施，比如避孕套，而你觉得作为女性，你的某一颗卵子可能已经被精子受精，它就会让你来月经。

segments.en: It makes you menstruate.
segments.zh: 它让你月经。

segments.en: That means the lining of your uterus and any egg, even if it was fertilized, comes out.
segments.zh: 这意味着你的子宫内膜以及任何卵子，即使已经受精，都会被排出。

segments.en: And in some cases, people think of it as a kind of abortion.
segments.zh: 在某些情况下，人们将其视为一种堕胎。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So yeah, it's very interesting how the more that we understand about medicine and about how life works, well, there have been advancements as well, like contraceptives that not only prevent unwanted pregnancies, but also prevent transmission of diseases, sexually transmitted diseases.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，很有意思，我们对医学和生命运作的了解越多，也出现了一些进步，比如避孕药不仅能防止意外怀孕，还能防止疾病传播，也就是性传播疾病。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: But at the same time, other things like this, like the emergency contraceptive and abortions start popping up.
segments.zh: 但与此同时，诸如紧急避孕药和堕胎之类的其他事情开始出现。

segments.en: So ethics.
segments.zh: 所以道德。

segments.en: Ethics, exactly.
segments.zh: 道德，确切地说。

segments.en: So a very interesting topic, as we said, controversial, but at the same time, very much beautiful, because we are talking about how our bodies work and how everyone came to existence.
segments.zh: 所以一个非常有趣的话题，正如我们所说，有争议，但同时，非常美丽，因为我们正在谈论我们的身体是如何运作的，以及每个人是如何出现的。

segments.en: And how babies are born.
segments.zh: 以及婴儿是如何出生的。

segments.en: Everyone loves babies.
segments.zh: 每个人都喜欢婴儿。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we're really interested to get your insights, your opinion about anything that we've talked about today.
segments.zh: 因此，我们非常有兴趣获得您的见解，您对我们今天讨论的任何内容的意见。

segments.en: And if you have any other questions or comments, you can always reach us at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何其他问题或意见，您可以随时通过 Englishpod.com 与我们联系。

segments.en: Yeah, we hope to see you there.
segments.zh: 是的，我们希望在那里见到你。

segments.en: And we hope this will start a nice conversation on our website.
segments.zh: 我们希望这将在我们的网站上开始愉快的对话。

segments.en: But remember, keep it clean.
segments.zh: 但记住，说话文明点。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we'll see everyone there.
segments.zh: 所以我们会在那里见到每个人。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: See you there.
segments.zh: 在那里见。
